hazards.control: Pressure test before pumping; bleed down and verify zero before breaking any connection.

name: Ball-drop frac sleeve
function: A casing or liner component with ports covered by an inner sleeve that a dropped ball shifts open, letting a stage be treated without perforating.

tabs.overview: Sleeves are run as part of the casing string, one per stage, with graduated ball seats: each ball is slightly larger than the last and passes every seat until its own. Landing on the seat, pressure shifts the sleeve open and the ball also isolates the stages below. After the job the seats are milled or the balls dissolve.
tabs.engineering: Seat sizes step by small increments, which limits the number of stages per string; seats are milled out to restore full bore.
tabs.connections: Threaded into the casing or liner string.
tabs.safety: No explosives; sleeve pressure rating is part of the string design.
tabs.evidence: Public plug-and-perf explainer (S20), API Spec 11D1 scope (S21), field practice (S9). Dimensions are public example values, not a manufacturer's design.
tabs.operations: Continuous pumping between stages; no wireline runs.
tabs.failure_modes: Ball passing its seat, sleeve failing to shift, seat erosion.
